questions.text: Which user segment is the primary design target today — is LLM KVCache the priority segment and Object/KV/stream/hetero secondary, or are they co-equal? (Product Owner)

Why was this bounded context built (business motivation) — is DataSystem a standalone product, a component extracted from the wider openYuanrong serverless engine, or a response to a specific customer/inference-cost problem? (Product Owner)
What are the success metrics / SLOs for this system — what numbers define success (e.g. p99 Get latency, throughput per GB-s, availability %)? (Product Owner)
What is the relative priority of the user segments — among Object / KV / stream / hetero, which scenario ranks first for roadmap and performance-tuning decisions? (Product Owner)
What are the authoritative acceptance criteria per use case — which observed system-test behaviours are contractual (definition of done, required error handling) versus incidental? (Product Owner)
What developer/operator usability outcome is required — what is the usability goal beyond one-command deploy and examples? (Product Owner)
Why embed the master in the worker process rather than running a standalone master tier? (Architect)
Why ZeroMQ for the primary RPC path when gRPC is also a dependency — was this a latency, framing-control, or gRPC-overhead decision? (Architect)

Which alternatives were actually evaluated (standalone vs embedded master; gRPC/brpc vs ZMQ; rendezvous vs consistent hashing; always-on vs optional RDMA), and how do they score against the quality goals? (Architect)
What are the quality requirements and the top-3 ISO-25010 quality attribute ranking for this product release/segment, and what are their target scenarios? (Architect)
Is Cedar authorization active at runtime in the request path, or is it planned / tooling-only? (Architect)

What is the security posture and threat model — is skip_authenticate ever permitted in production, what is the isolation model (multi-tenant vs external attacker), are there compliance frameworks, and is audit logging mandated? (Architect)
What are the quantified scaling limits (maximum nodes per cluster, objects/keys per worker, object size) that bound the scaling design? (Architect)
Where is technical debt formally tracked — Gitee/GitCode issues, an internal backlog, or another registry — so Phase 2 can cite open debt items? (Developer)
What real-world problem and domain drove building a near-compute multi-level cache — which workloads and cost pressures define the domain? (Domain Expert)
Are there business-specific terms not defined in the code (SLA tiers, workload names, customer-facing concepts) that must enter the architecture glossary? (Domain Expert)
From an operations standpoint: is audit logging required, at what granularity, and are there compliance obligations governing deployment? (Operations)
What availability target must the cluster meet, and what is the required behaviour/tolerance when ETCD is unavailable or clocks skew? (Operations)

answers.Q1.2.motivation: LLM KVCache is the priority segment today; Object/KV/stream/hetero interfaces are the enabling primitives underneath it and are treated as secondary from a roadmap-tuning standpoint.
answers.Q1.4: DataSystem is a component extracted from the wider openYuanrong Serverless engine, hardened into a semi-standalone cache to attack NPU inference-cluster data-sharing cost; it can ship alone but was born inside the platform.
answers.Q1.5: single-digit-µs shared-memory Get, multi-GB/s per-node D2D/H2D throughput, ≥99.9% worker availability, and sub-few-second failover.
answers.Q1.6: Hetero-object (HBM KVCache) ranks first for performance tuning; KV second, Object third, stream last as an opportunistic surface.
answers.Q2.5: successful zero-copy Set/Get, correct refcount/TTL lifecycle, and defined error codes on miss/OOM/failover; timing and internal replica placement observed in tests are incidental.
answers.Q4.4-target: Beyond one-command deploy, the usability goal is a single-node-equivalent programming experience — SDK calls hide sharding, placement, and transport so app developers never reason about the cluster.
answers.Q3.9.EmbeddedMaster.Rationale: The master is embedded in the worker to avoid an extra network hop and a separate failure/scaling tier; metadata co-locates with the data it governs, and ETCD supplies the cross-node coordination.
answers.Q3.9.ZmqTransport.Rationale: ZeroMQ was chosen for the hot RPC path for framing control and lower per-message overhead than gRPC; gRPC remains for management/control-plane calls where its ergonomics outweigh its cost.
answers.Q3.9.PughMatrix: embedded vs standalone master (embedded won on latency/ops simplicity), ZMQ vs gRPC/brpc (ZMQ won on hot-path overhead), consistent hashing vs rendezvous (consistent hashing won on rebalance cost), optional vs always-on RDMA (optional, since TCP is the current baseline).
answers.Q3.8.Cedar: Cedar authorization is planned/tooling-only; it is not yet enforced in the runtime request path.
answers.Q4.6.target: Threat model is trusted-cluster internal abuse; skip_authenticate is a dev/test convenience not sanctioned for production, isolation is single-tenant-per-cluster, no formal compliance framework applies, and audit logging is best-effort.
answers.Q5.5-limits: hundreds of worker nodes per cluster, millions of keys per worker, and object sizes from bytes up to multi-GB shards.
answers.Q5.1.TrackedDebt: Formal debt lives in the GitCode/Gitee issue tracker plus .repo_context/roadmap.md; in-code FIXMEs are not the system of record.
answers.Q1.4.shared: Driven by LLM long-sequence inference: KVCache reuse and Prefill/Decode transfer pressure made re-fetching/recomputing across nodes the dominant cost, motivating a near-compute HBM/DRAM/SSD cache.
answers.Q3.12-glossary: Yes: terms like heterogeneous object, WRITE_BACK/WRITE_THROUGH tiers, Causal/PRAM consistency modes, and hot-replica need glossary entries as customer-facing concepts not fully self-evident from code.
answers.Q4.6.target.shared: Audit logging is best-effort at connection/auth granularity, not mandated; no external compliance obligation currently governs deployment beyond internal platform policy.
answers.Q5.3-target: Target ≥99.9% cluster availability; on ETCD unavailability the cluster holds last-known metadata read-only and pauses rebalancing, and clock skew is tolerated via lease-based rather than absolute-time expiry.
answers.Q3.10: Reliability, then Performance Efficiency, then Usability — targeted respectively at failover/recovery, KVCache throughput/latency, and single-machine-style SDK experience.
answers.Q4.9: Reliability, then Performance Efficiency, then Usability — targeted respectively at failover/recovery, KVCache throughput/latency, and single-machine-style SDK experience.
